title: Context Refresh Runbook
summary: This resource helps a practitioner determine whether a context-refresh guide can be corrected safely after a cited source moves or passes its review cadence. The substantive refresh mechanism remains UNKNOWN until the existing guide and an authoritative topical source are available.
prerequisites: The previous citation metadata and source history
An authoritative source describing the applicable context-refresh mechanism
Access to the catalogue identifier registry and resource validation process

sections.title: Answer and change status
paragraphs: Can you safely correct the context-refresh runbook from the available source record? UNKNOWN. Do not make a substantive correction until you have the current resource, its previous source metadata, and an authoritative source that defines the relevant context-refresh mechanism.

This is an intermediate-level resource. It assumes that the reader can compare repository content and inspect source metadata, but it does not assume knowledge of any provider-specific context mechanism.

The only prior citation identified is content/resources/prompting-context/context-refresh-runbook.json, recorded with an unregistered publisher and no verification date. Whether that citation moved, exceeded a defined review cadence, or experienced both conditions is UNKNOWN because its prior URL, source contents, redirect target, and cadence were not supplied.

What changed in the cited source and which existing statements or procedures it affected are also UNKNOWN. No substantive context-refresh claim or procedure is corrected here because asserting one would require unsupported information. Whether unaffected wording has remained unchanged is UNKNOWN because the existing file was not supplied for comparison.
sections.callout: The safe answer is to stop the substantive update until the baseline and authoritative topical evidence are available.

sections.title: Correction procedure
paragraphs: First, retrieve the verbatim current resource and its previous committed state. If either state is unavailable, stop the correction and request the missing repository content rather than reconstructing it from the filename or work-item description.

Second, inspect the existing sources array and source history to identify the prior URL, publisher, verification date, and review cadence. If those records do not establish which source triggered the review, record the trigger as UNKNOWN and obtain the missing source history before editing substantive text.

Third, open the authoritative replacement or refreshed source and compare it with the source version on which the guide was based. If the source cannot be opened directly over HTTPS, do not claim that it was verified; locate an accessible first-party replacement or escalate the unresolved citation for editorial review.

Fourth, record the specific source change and map it to the exact statements or procedure steps that depend on it. If the old and current source contents cannot be compared, leave the affected guide material unchanged and request a source snapshot or documented change history.

Fifth, correct only the mapped statements, their associated remediation paths, and the necessary source metadata. If a corrected procedure step can fail, state its observable failure condition and a supported next action; if authoritative documentation does not establish that next action, omit the step and mark the remediation UNKNOWN in the review record.

Finally, compare the corrected file with the baseline. If the comparison shows unrelated wording, metadata, ordering, or formatting changes, revert those changes and repeat the comparison until only the supported correction remains.

sections.title: Expected evidence and verification
paragraphs: The expected evidence is the original resource, the previous source record, the accessible authoritative source reviewed for the correction, a note identifying what changed and what text it affected, and a comparison containing no unrelated edits. If any item is missing, treat the correction as incomplete and obtain the missing evidence before publication.

Verify that the final file parses as one JSON object, contains only fields permitted by the Resource schema, and uses the required identifier derived from the target filename. If parsing fails, correct the reported JSON syntax error and parse the complete file again.

Verify identifier uniqueness against the complete catalogue registry. If the identifier is already assigned to another item, stop publication and refer the collision to the catalogue owner rather than selecting a new identifier without approval.

Verify every final source by opening its HTTPS URL and reviewing the cited material on the date recorded in its lastVerified field. If a URL redirects, is unavailable, or does not support the associated claim, replace it with a directly accessible authoritative source and repeat the review. Direct URL resolution for the sources listed here is CANNOT VERIFY in the drafting environment because network access is unavailable.

A successful correction is one for which the changed source, substantive change, affected text, supported remediation paths, source-review dates, schema validation, identifier check, and minimal comparison are all documented. That result is currently UNKNOWN because the original resource, topical source history, catalogue registry, and network-enabled source checks were not supplied.
